technical_summary: The 6U weather-monitoring cubesat employs a microwave radiometer payload for atmospheric moisture and temperature profiling, complemented by visible/IR imagers for cloud cover analysis. The mission targets a 500 km sun-synchronous orbit with 2-year operational lifetime. The spacecraft uses a 3-axis stabilized ADCS with reaction wheels and magnetorquers, S-band uplink/X-band downlink communications, and deployable solar arrays generating 60W average power. Key technical drivers include thermal management of the radiometer focal plane, RF interference mitigation between payload and bus systems, and strict mass/CG constraints for P-POD compatibility. The design emphasizes protoflight qualification to minimize schedule risk.

payload_summary.thermal_control: Passive radiators + thermoelectric cooler for focal plane (< -40°C)

adcs.sensors: Star tracker (0.01° accuracy), MEMS gyros, magnetometer, sun sensors

propulsion.deorbit: 25 m² drag sail (deploys at EOL), <25 year deorbit compliance

ground_support_equipment.mechanical: P-POD fit check fixture, mass properties measurement rig
ground_support_equipment.electrical: EGSE with simulated power bus, command/telemetry interface
ground_support_equipment.thermal: Thermal vacuum chamber with LN2 shroud (-100°C to +100°C)
ground_support_equipment.rf: RF anechoic chamber, spectrum analyzer, vector network analyzer
ground_support_equipment.software: Mission control software simulators, ground station emulator

environmental_test_schedule.criteria: ±1 mm clearance on all sides, smooth rail insertion

environmental_test_schedule.purpose: Verify no interference between payload and bus
environmental_test_schedule.criteria: Meet MIL-STD-461G RE102/CE102, payload noise < -120 dBm
No mechanical failure, post-test functional OK

environmental_test_schedule.purpose: Verify response at launch vehicle frequencies

environmental_test_schedule.criteria: All functions nominal, no outgassing contamination
Performance within spec, mass loss <1% TML, <0.1% CVCM

environmental_test_schedule.purpose: Verify antenna patterns and link budget
Verify solar panel and antenna deployment
environmental_test_schedule.criteria: Full deployment in <30s, no binding, latch confirmation

integration_and_test_plan.critical_path: Thermal vacuum → RF acceptance → Final functional

constraints.debris: No loose parts, all fasteners captured or tethered

deployment_sequence.trigger: Deployer door opens after 30 min on orbit
deployment_sequence.clearance: Minimum 10 cm from deployer before any activation

critical_milestones_and_schedule.recommended_margin: 3 months contingency (16.7%) distributed across integration and test phases

key_risks_and_mitigations.risk: Thermal control of radiometer focal plane
key_risks_and_mitigations.impact: High - Payload performance degradation or failure
mitigation: Early thermal vacuum testing of focal plane assembly
Design margin: TEC capacity 2× worst-case heat load
Redundant temperature sensors with independent control loops
Ground testing with flight-like vacuum and temperature profiles

key_risks_and_mitigations.risk: RF interference between X-band downlink and radiometer receivers
mitigation: Early EMC testing with both systems operating
Frequency planning: 200 MHz guard band between payload and downlink
Shielded enclosures for sensitive analog circuits
Time-domain scheduling: No downlink during critical observation periods
Early fit check with actual P-POD fixture (not just drawings)
3D scanning of flight structure before final machining
Design margin: 2 mm clearance minimum (vs 1 mm requirement)
Vibration testing with P-POD interface simulator
Redundant deployment mechanisms (primary spring + backup actuator)
Ground testing with thermal vacuum and vibration pre-conditioning
Design for single-fault tolerance in deployment circuit
In-orbit contingency: Use body-mounted panels as backup

key_risks_and_mitigations.risk: ADCS pointing accuracy insufficient for radiometer
mitigation: Early testing with engineering model in 3-axis air bearing
Design margin: 0.1° control (vs 0.5° requirement)
On-orbit calibration using star tracker and ground targets
Software updates to improve control algorithms post-launch

key_risks_and_mitigations.risk: Schedule slip due to parts procurement delays
key_risks_and_mitigations.impact: Medium - Increased cost, missed launch window
mitigation: Dual-source critical components (OBC, radios, reaction wheels)
Early procurement of long-lead items (12+ month lead time)
Buffer stock of common components
Flexible design allowing substitution of equivalent parts

key_action: Immediately procure P-POD Mk III interface fixture and conduct first mechanical fit check with engineering model structure to validate mechanical design and identify any clearance issues before CDR. This gates all subsequent structural fabrication and is the highest schedule risk item.
